what: The lab's own reads of FLOP devnet around its runtime upgrade from spec 1014014 to spec 1014020. Read only: no transaction was sent.
method: chain_getBlockHash, chain_getBlock, state_getRuntimeVersion, state_getMetadata, state_getStorage (System.LastRuntimeUpgrade, System.Events, Timestamp.Now), state_getStorageHash and state_getStorageSize of the :code key, each at the block's hash. what_changed_in_the_metadata.method: Two readings that share no code. First, the lab's own strict metadata parser (observatory/src/scale/metadata.ts): for every pallet its index, every call, event and error with its index (calls and events with their field names and type names), every storage entry with its modifier and hashers, every constant with its value, and the extrinsic version and signed extensions; then a comparison of the two lists. Second, an agent's comparison with the reference decoder (@polkadot-api/substrate-bindings 0.21.2), types compared by structure, never by id. Both give the same 39 differences.

what_changed_in_the_metadata.differences_note: ADDED, CHANGED and REMOVED are from spec 1014014 to spec 1014020. Field types are the names the metadata gives. The outer call and event types of the runtime grow with these entries, so every type that holds a call or an event (Utility.batch, Sudo.sudo, FlopSessionKeys.execute_via_session, System.Events) changes with them and in no other way: that is the second reading's result.

the_lab_signers.result: Every call they encode has the same pallet index, call index and fields at both specs. The signed extensions, the extrinsic version, the transaction version (2) and the storage keys they read are the same. So they sign valid bytes for spec 1014020 with only the spec version changed (a flag they already take).
the_lab_signers.source: the second reading, which matched each of the 16 call shapes and 9 storage keys field by field against both metadata blobs. The first reading agrees for every name, index and field type name. Read, not run: no transaction was sent at spec 1014020.
the_lab_signers.what_this_does_not_show: Whether the chain accepts these calls at spec 1014020, or does the same thing with them. Metadata holds no logic.

error_indexes_moved.consequence: A failed call names its error by pallet index and error index. A table of error names made from the 1014014 metadata misnames FlopSessionKeys errors 16 to 18 and HwCalibration errors 6 to 15 at spec 1014020. The session escrow test recorded SpendExceedsDeclared as error 18; the same refusal at spec 1014020 would carry 20. The observatory's decoder gives an error's indexes and never its name, and its reviewed shape states no errors, so the shape diff says nothing about this by design.

what_changed_in_the_metadata.correction: An earlier version of the README in this folder said the new metadata adds the call set_model_mirrors. That was wrong. ModelRegistry.set_model_mirrors is call 21 in both runtimes. The calls this upgrade adds are ComputeChannel.set_capacity_reservation_rate (50) and ComputeChannel.drop_capacity_reservation (51).

not_read: No event of spec 1014020 was decoded in this folder: the observatory's tests on its third recording do that. Whether any storage was migrated at block 3528529 was not read. Nothing here shows that the lab's session tests of 2026-11-11 give the same results at spec 1014020: only a rerun shows behaviour. The two extrinsics were read by position, not by a decoder: the lab has none for extrinsics. The signatures on them were not checked. How the authorization was decided off chain is not on chain.
